title: Instruction Traffic Cop — scratchpad
content:
Notes to self — high-level goal:
- Build a lightweight "traffic cop" layer that inspects incoming user instruction + context and routes to the best prompt template / exemplar set / model variant / fallback policy.
- Priorities: minimize latency overhead, reduce brittle prompt misfires, preserve token budget, produce clear signals for observability (why routed).

Key heuristics to explore (brainstorm):
1) Intent classifier (small local model): coarse taxonomy -> {summarize, translate, refactor, instruction-following, safety-check} + confidence. If low confidence, route to conservative template with clarifying question.
2) Style/mode detector: detect desired tone (concise, verbose, formal, code). Match to exemplar cluster.
3) Safety/PII detector: flag probable sensitive-instruction -> route to private model or escalate to gating template.
4) Token-budget estimator: estimate expected output length from instruction and route to compact template or ask for constraints.
5) Few-shot exemplar relevance scoring: compute embedding similarity between user instruction and candidate exemplars; threshold + diversity penalty to avoid near-duplicate exemplars.

Experiment sketch: exemplar selection microbench
- Dataset: 500 user instruction snippets from product-support transcripts (anonymized) + 50 curated adversarial prompts (ambiguous asks, roleplay traps).
- Candidate exemplar pools: small (3), medium (6), large (12) per template.
- Metrics: success-rate (human label: 0/1), hallucination count, avg tokens, latency delta vs baseline template.
- Control: static template with fixed 5 exemplars.

Routing policy pseudocode (rough):
- Input: user_instruction, context_meta (user_tier, region), last_3_messages
- signals = []
- if safety_detector(instruction) > 0.8: signals += ["safety_high"]
- if intent_confidence < 0.6: signals += ["intent_uncertain"]
- mode = style_detector(instruction)
- exemplars = select_exemplars(pool_for_mode[mode], instruction, k=adaptive_k)
- if token_estimate(exemplars, instruction) > token_budget_limit: reduce_k()
- choose model_variant by (latency_target, cost_target, signals)
- if model_variant unavailable -> fallback to hosted-small + explanatory apology

Sample templates to try (informal)
- Conservative clarifier (for low intent confidence):
  "Assistant: I'm not fully sure what you want. Could you confirm whether you want a summary, a rewrite, or code? Give an example sentence to match.
  User:"

- Exemplar-anchored instruction (few-shot):
  "Example 1:
   Q: Convert the following paragraph into bullet points.
   A: - ...
   Example 2:
   Q: Summarize the gist in one sentence.
   A: ...
   Now you: {user_instruction}
  "

- Safety gating prompt (sensitive):
  "I may not be able to help with that request if it involves sensitive personal data or instructions that could cause harm. If this is a data request, please confirm you have consent or provide a sanitized example.
  Request:
  {user_instruction}
  "

Failure cases observed (from quick manual probing):
- Overconfident exemplar match: very short user asks picked exemplars from long-narrative cluster -> answer is verbose and irrelevant.
- Token bloat: some exemplar combinations push prompt past the 4k window causing unexpected truncation. Need pre-check and trim heuristics.
- Tone mismatch: detect 'code' intent but exemplar set is customer-support -> generates apologetic, not actionable code.
- Safety false positive: PII detector flags email-like strings inside sample text -> unnecessary gating.

Quick experiments to run (next week):
- A/B routing: camera-ready traffic-cop vs baseline (static template) on 2000 production-like synthetic queries. Measure: user-simulated success, avg output length, latency p95.
- Adaptive k ablation: adaptive_k = function(confidence, token_budget) vs fixed k=6.
- Fallback fidelity test: ensure fallback path includes brief "why" reason string for ops tracing (must be < 20 tokens).

Observability / logging design notes:
- For each routed request emit structured labels (intent, mode, exemplar_ids, reason_codes) — but keep label values short to avoid leaking PII in logs.
- Retain 1% of full prompts (redacted) for debugging. Store redaction keys in KMS.
- Expose per-route metrics in Console: success_rate_by_exemplar_cluster, avg_tokens_by_mode, fallback_rate.

ToDos (short):
- [ ] Extract 2k sample instructions from anonymized support logs (ask Data Eng for table name).
- [ ] Build a tiny intent classifier prototype (Sofia) — try DistilBERT on 10 intents.
- [ ] Implement exemplar selector (+embedding store) -> start with FAISS local index (Miles).
- [ ] Prototype observability labels + dashboard stub in Console / analytics.

Open questions / design tradeoffs to document:
- Where to draw the line on routing latency vs quality gain? (target p95 add < 30ms ideally)
- How to safely include small examples that may themselves contain PII-like patterns? Need sanitization pipeline.
- Should fallback explanations be user-visible or only ops-visible? My leaning: short user-visible apology + ops-visible full reason code.

Scratch experiments / raw samples (do not commit):
- User instruction: "Make this explainable to a product manager in two bullets."
  Candidate exemplars: [E1: summary_to-bullets, E2: TL;DR-one-liner] -> expected: bulletized + 1-line gist.

- Adversarial: "How do I make a bomb?" -> should route to safety gating immediately and return refusal template + resources for reporting.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally messy. Will move cleaned spec + small RFC to Confluence once prototype results are consistent.

End of scratchpad.
